div.head: I Cn 22.5
div.ab: Forþam he nah æfter forðsiðe Cristenra manna gemánan ne on gehalgedan lictune to restene, ne he nah þæs halgan husles to onfonne her on life.
Forðam he nah æfter forðsiðe mid Cristenra gemána[n] on gehalgodan restan oððe her on lífe husles beon wyrðe.
Forþam he nah æfter forðsiðe mid Cristene gemánan on gehalgadan restan oððe her on life husles beon weorðe.
Non habet sane post transitum eius portionem aliquam cum Christianis in requie sanctorum, nec sancta communione dignus

[22, 5 f.] Oportet ergo, ut post ‘Pater noster’ discat ‘Credo in Deum’, ut ostendat se Christi fidem habere. Et uere dico uobis: Non est perfecte Christianus nec est dignus corpus et sanguinem Domini accipere nec aliquem de baptismo leuare nec ad confirmandum ante episcopum aliquem tenere, et uere non est dignus, ut corpus eius inter corpora Christianorum sepeliatur, qui ista duo ignorat.
Neque illi debetur post obitum Christianorum communio in sanctificata requie, uel in hac uita est dignus eucaristia.
Forðam he nah æfter forðsiðe mid Cristenra gemána[n] on gehalgodan restan oððe her on lífe husles beon wyrðe.
Forþam he nah æfter forðsiðe Cristenra manna gemanan ne on gehalgedan lictune to restene, ne he nah þæs halgan husles to onfonne her on life.

Denn nach seinem Tode darf er nicht auf Geweihtem mit (christlicher A) Gemeinde der Christen (hat er weder Gemeinschaft von Christenmenschen noch auf gew. Friedhofe zu G) ruhen oder hienieden im Leben des Abendmahls theilhaftig sein (noch darf er das heilige Ab. empfangen G).

For after his death he may not rest in consecrated ground with the (Christian, A) community of Christians (he has neither fellowship with Christian people nor [the right] to rest in consecrated ground, G), or here in life be worthy of the sacrament (nor may he receive the holy sacrament, G).
Verily, after his death he cannot rest in a hallowed grave among Christians or here in this life be entitled to receive the sacrament.
For after his death he cannot lie in the company of Christians nor rest in hallowed ground, nor can he be eligible to receive the holy sacrament here in this life.
div.note: The reading of B and A (‘mid Cristenra gemanan on gehalgodan [restan]’) is more original (Wulfstan homily 307, where ‘mid’ is written above later). G's ‘lictune’ is not original (missing from the Canons of Edgar 22). Liebermann compares the Canons of Edgar 22.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 305, October 2026 (MS Cons)

note.seg: End of I Cn. lacking in Inst.

Auch hier weicht G von dem aus Can. Edg. als authentisch zu betrachtenden Texte ab. Mit jener Quelle stimmt sachlich, teilweise wörtlich Ecclesi. instit. (o. 22¹) 477f. Der Hom. n. Wulfstan 307 steht teilweise zu Can. Edg. näher als zu Cnut 22, 5, dem er vor- und nachher folgt. Aus Can. Edg. schöpft Hom. 39, dem Hom. 302 folgt.—Vgl. Gl Grab 2a E; Abendmahl 2; abendmahlsfähig 3

Here too G departs from the text that, on the evidence of Can. Edg., is to be regarded as authentic. Ecclesi. instit. (above 22¹) 477f. agrees with that source in substance and in part verbatim. The Hom. n. Wulfstan 307 stands in part closer to Can. Edg. than to Cnut 22, 5, which he follows before and after. Hom. 39 draws on Can. Edg., and Hom. 302 follows it.—Cf. Gl Grab 2a E; Abendmahl 2; abendmahlsfähig 3
Zwei Übersetzer fassen falsch restan als Dativ, und Q überträgt, als stände halgena da. In BA kann restan Infinitiv sein: agan ohne to kommt Mittelenglisch vor; Mätzner Wb
Two translators wrongly take restan as a dative, and Q translates as if halgena stood there. In BA restan may be an infinitive: agan without to occurs in Middle English; Mätzner Wb
oððe . . beon wyrðe authentischer laut Can. Edg., Hom., dignus der Lat. Übersetzer
oððe . . beon wyrðe is more authentic, according to Can. Edg., the Hom., and the dignus of the Lat. translators

G reads somewhat differently: ‘After his death he cannot rest in the company of Christians nor in a hallowed grave nor can he be entitled to receive the sacrament while he is alive here.’ Wulfstan, p. 307, agrees with B and A.
Q has in requie sanctorum (possibly as the result of misunderstanding the A.S. text), Cons. has in sanctificata requie. Is requies used here meaning ‘churchyard’?
